title: Project per-option mechanics for option-catalog features (e.g. Eldritch Invocations) instead of a blunt top-level scan
description:
Follow-up from eshyra-o9bd.19.2.1.3.1 (splitting the composed subrace ASI
text and the Eldritch Invocations option list into verbatim spans).

Context: feature:warlock:eldritch-invocations' data.description previously
contained the feature's own body PLUS the (wrongly joined) end-of-chapter
option-list text for all 32 invocations. deriveFeatureMechanics scans
data.description as one blob, so mechanics phrases physically located
inside individual invocation option bodies (a long-rest resource reset,
blinded/deafened/invisible condition mentions, a Deception/Persuasion
proficiency grant) were picked up and attached to the FEATURE's single
top-level data.mechanics block, misattributed (not scoped to which
invocation actually grants them).

eshyra-o9bd.19.2.1.3.1 correctly split that option-list text out into a new
data.optionCatalog field (kept apart from description, matching how the SRD
actually prints it). deriveFeatureMechanics is only ever called on
description, so after the split feature:warlock:eldritch-invocations now
has NO mechanics block at all (missingCount for feature.mechanics rose
48 -> 49 in test/srdGeneratedPack.test.ts's EXPECTED_PARTIAL_FIELDS). This
is more truthful than before (the old block was misattributed to the whole
feature, not any specific invocation), but it also means no invocation's
mechanics are projected anywhere structurally.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR (design decision needed, not made here): decide whether
per-invocation-option mechanics should be derived — most naturally by
running mechanics projection per option in
deriveFeatureChoices.ts's parseOptionCatalog (each DerivedChoiceOption
already isolates one invocation's own text), attaching to
choices[].options[].mechanics or similar — or whether this is out of
scope/acceptable given invocations are typically spell-like grants better
modeled via existing spellGrants machinery. Some invocations (e.g. Devil's
Sight -> darkvision-like sense, Beguiling Influence -> proficiency grant)
look like clean mechanics-projection candidates; others are cast-at-will
spell grants already covered by a different mechanism worth checking first.

LIKELY FILES: packages/core/scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/deriveFeatureChoices.ts
(parseOptionCatalog), mechanicsProjections.ts (deriveFeatureMechanics),
kindSchemas.ts (option mechanics shape if added), and the OPTION_CATALOG_SPECS
list (fighting-style, metamagic, pact-boon, hunters-prey, defensive-tactics,
multiattack, superior-hunters-defense) which share the same blind spot for
any future case where an option's own body carries mechanics-bearing prose.

Not a correctness regression from eshyra-o9bd.19.2.1.3.1 — nothing in src/
or test/ currently reads feature:warlock:eldritch-invocations' top-level
mechanics block; this is a coverage/completeness gap being surfaced, not a
fix that broke a live consumer.
